title: MAGIS: Memory Optimization via Coordinated Graph Transformation and Scheduling for DNN
problem: Deep neural networks have rapidly increasing memory consumption from large tensor shapes and long lifetimes. Existing graph scheduling approaches for memory optimization significantly reduce performance and can only manipulate tensor lifetimes, not shapes, limiting the optimization space.
motivation: Memory consumption is a critical bottleneck for deploying deep neural networks on resource-constrained hardware.
method: MAGIS jointly applies graph transformation (which modifies tensor shapes and graph structure) and graph scheduling (which determines operator execution and tensor movement timings). By coordinating these techniques, it exploits new memory-performance trade-off space created by shape modifications, which prior separate applications of these techniques could not leverage.
key_novelty: Coordinating graph transformation with scheduling to jointly optimize memory and performance by exploiting tensor shape modification trade-offs.
contributions: Identifies that graph transformation and scheduling should be coordinated for improved memory-performance optimization
Proposes MAGIS system that jointly applies graph transformation and scheduling
Demonstrates new memory-performance trade-off space through coordinated tensor shape and execution timing optimization
primary_theme: coordinated graph transformation and scheduling for DNN memory optimization
